episodes.168837: A passing cold frontal zone combined with a hot and humid air mass to produce numerous afternoon thunderstorms across south-central and southeastern central Indiana...with one report of wind damage in Rush County.
episodes.168861: A nearly stationary boundary oriented from north to south set up over the area. Showers and thunderstorms developed along the boundary. Storm motion was also north to south, which allowed for storms to train over the same locations, resulting in instances of flooding and flash flooding.
episodes.168907: A surge of moisture from Tropical Storm Celia which was off the west coast of Mexico near 17N moved over a hot and unstable airmass which was situated over central California. This resulted in scattered showers and thunderstorms over the area on June 22 which was also the first significant precipitation event for the area in two months.  Due to the convective nature of the precipitation, rainfall amounts varied; but a few thunderstorms produced one to two tenths of an inch of rainfall in the San Joaquin Valley.  Some stations in the Tehachapi Mountains and the south end of the upper Sierra picked up between a  quarter and three quarters of an inch of rainfall.  Some of the thunderstorms produced strong outflow winds and dry microbursts which resulted in several trees and power lines being downed.
episodes.169024: An upper-level trough situated just off the California Coast resulted in an influx of moisture into southeast California. Showers and thunderstorms developed in the afternoon hours across the eastern half of Riverside County with a northward motion. Heavy rainfall, which resulted in flash flooding just north of Desert Center damaging a law enforcement vehicle, as well as blowing dust from outward propagating outflows were the primarily hazards from these storms. No injuries were reported.
episodes.169036: The surface synoptic set-up on June 22, 2022 was similar to that of the severe weather event just 6 days earlier, as a north-south stationary boundary bisected central Pennsylvania ahead of a cold front approaching from the Great Lakes. To the west of the north-south stationary boundary, the airmass over western Pennsylvania was very warm and humid with strong instability. Scattered thunderstorms first developed during the early afternoon over the south-central mountains, with additional activity developing farther north over the central mountains and over western Pennsylvania later in the afternoon.  By early evening, the primary focus for convection was found just ahead of the front as it pushed into western Pennsylvania. Damaging winds were the dominant severe weather type, with only one report of marginally severe hail. One thunderstorm brought locally heavy rain to Altoona and Hollidaysburg resulting in minor flooding.
episodes.169093: A strongly unstable airmass in a moderately sheared environment squeezed between two fronts resulted in several clusters of destructive thunderstorms. The most intense thunderstorms propagated north to south along a stalled front dividing very unstable air near and west of Interstate 95, from notably more stable air closer to the Chesapeake Bay.||The event was unusual not only because of the intensity of the thunderstorms, but because they moved in a north to south direction, even propagating south-southwestward at times.

episodes.169134: Widespread thunderstorm activity occurred on June 21-22. Multiple small wildfires were started due to lightning strikes, and localized flooding was reported.
episodes.169228: A strong dust devil developed and caused property damage in Battle Mountain.
episodes.169355: Strong storms that produced damaging winds developed the evening of June 22, 2022. A broken line of showers and storms developed between Cleveland and Pittsburgh just before 3pm and continue to advances southeast along the axis of a trough entering from the north. Dry conditions under ridging hours ahead of the showers and storms helped prime the environment. Mean level CAPE before convective was between 3000-3500J/kg, and steep lapse rates near the surface (7.5 to 8.0C/km) help with strong damaging updrafts.

episodes.169742: A surface low situated over the Great Lakes tracked eastward toward New England, with a trailing cold front that pushed eastward towards the Commonwealth. SPC had eastern Kentucky in a marginal category for severe weather throughout the day, with the main threat being wind. A watch was issued for the forecast area in the late afternoon before severe storms associated with the front moved through.
episodes.169880: A broken line of severe thunderstorms moved through Iowa and Illinois the evening of June 21st. These produced heavy rain totals and areas of damaging winds, especially in Iowa.
episodes.169882: A broken line of severe thunderstorms moved through Iowa and Illinois the evening of June 21st. These produced heavy rain totals and areas of damaging winds, especially in Iowa.
episodes.170159: On the afternoon of June 22nd, a cold front made eastward progress into the Middle Ohio Valley, which served as the main contributor behind strong to severe thunderstorms in West Virginia. Optimal moisture levels and warm temperatures ahead of the front helped to promote these storms by the early afternoon on the 22nd, which spanned into the evening time frame as well. ||While an instance of quarter sized hail was observed in Nicholas County, the bulk of the strong to severe storms resulted in damaging wind gusts that knocked down trees in several areas across the state. Heavier downpours also caused high water to be observed along local roadwyas in Nicholas and Barbour Counties.
episodes.170164: Strong to severe thunderstorms ahead of a cold front led to numerous areas of downed trees for the second half of the day on June 22nd. One storm in particular brought upon severe damage to a local community in Athens County involving homes, trees, and power lines. Storms came to an end later that evening as the cold front completed its passage over southeast Ohio.
episodes.170239: A cold front encroaching on the Lower Ohio Valley on the warm and muggy day of June 22nd led to strong thunderstorms developing in eastern Kentucky. Storms were primarily driven by daytime heating and quickly diminished after sunset as the front pressed eastward. The strongest storms steered away from eastern Kentucky, but there were two instances of single trees down in Greenup and Lawrence Counties.
episodes.170576: In the community of Pico Rivera, a lightning strike killed a woman who was walking her dogs.
episodes.170734: A cluster of severe storms moved into eastern Kansas and eventually through the Kansas City Metro during the evening hours on June 21. Mostly 60 to 65 mph wind was reported with some minor damage.
episodes.170735: A few clusters of storms moved into northern Missouri and eventually into west central Missouri. Generally, reports of 60 to 65 mph winds were reported with minor damage from those winds.
episodes.170869: Several reports of damaging wind occurred during the late evening hours of 6/21 as scattered strong storms moved across the area.
episodes.170937: A line of thunderstorms along a cold front produced strong winds and tree damage in some areas across southern WI.
episodes.171012: A weak cold front moved through the Ohio Valley on June 22nd, with showers and thunderstorms developing just ahead of the front during the afternoon hours. Across southern Indiana, a cluster of disorganized showers and thunderstorms intensified and merged into a line as they approached the Ohio River. Ahead of the cold front, temperatures surged into the mid-90s with dewpoints in the low-to-mid 70s, and storms had large amounts of instability to work with. Storms intensified enough to produce severe wind damage, mainly across Clark and Floyd County before crossing the Ohio River into central Kentucky.
episodes.171150: Unusually deep moisture for late June was located over southwest New Mexico with some slow moving storms dropping significant rains across the area which led to flash flooding around Mesquite and Hillsboro.
episodes.171381: A broken line of showers and thunderstorms formed along a weak cold front which moved across central Kentucky during the afternoon and evening on June 22nd. Ahead of the front, temperatures surged into the mid-90s with dewpoint temperatures in the low-to-mid 70s, creating a highly unstable environment which helped to grow and sustain storms through the evening hours. As the storms moved across central and eastern Kentucky, they produced wind damage mainly along a leading gust front which helped organize storms through the evening. Strong to severe storms continued to push southward into the Lake Cumberland region, producing more wind damage before moving into Tennessee and dissipating.
episodes.171512: Storms moved through north central and south central Kansas during the evening hours. These storms produced 60 to 70 mph winds and damage. Additionally there were reports of up to golf ball sized hail.
episodes.171513: Some severe thunderstorms moved through south central Kansas during the late afternoon and evening. They produced 60 to 80 mph winds and hail up to the size of golf balls. Damage to trees and roofs occurred with this activity.
episodes.171597: A short wave trough, out ahead of an approaching cold front, crossed the area during the afternoon and triggered showers and thunderstorms along the lake breeze boundaries. A thunderstorm that developed over the Niagara Peninsula slowly tracked southeast becoming better organized and expanding in size. This storm crossed over the Buffalo Metro, then it proceeded to the southeast. Wind damage was eventually reported from this storm in Cattaraugus County. Up until that point, weaker activity had crossed along the Lake Ontario shoreline, resulting in one wind report near Irondequoit.
episodes.171598: A short wave trough, out ahead of an approaching cold front, crossed the area during the afternoon and triggered showers and thunderstorms along the lake breeze boundaries. episodes.171652: Scattered severe thunderstorms well in advance of a cold front produced damaging winds across portions of central and south central Virginia.
episodes.171661: Scattered thunderstorms well in advance of a cold front produced gusty winds across portions of the James River.
episodes.171663: Scattered thunderstorms well in advance of a cold front produced gusty winds across portions of the Chesapeake Bay.
episodes.171699: CAPE values of over 1000 J/kg with DCAPE about the same allowed for severe wind gusts.  Shear was weak and lapse rates were modest at best so most storms were below severe limits.
episodes.171830: A weakening cold front approaching the area from the Ohio River Valley interacted with an unstable environment in southwest Virginia to spawn scattered severe thunderstorms. A few of the storms in the Virginia Piedmont produced damaging winds.
